$\pi_{54}(S^9)$, $k=45$, $n=9$: open. Theorem 5.3 (1) (p. 53, PDF 60) has a removable simple unstable element at $(n,k)=(9,45)$ ($AB_2$ above the dot, $B_2$ below it), so mod A $\pi^9_{54}\supseteq\mathbf Z/9\oplus\mathbf Z/3$; the table of §5.6 (p. 61) at $k=45$, $n=9$ shows only the $\circ$ of $\varphi$, that is $\mathbf Z/9$. The stem $45\equiv1\pmod4$ has no alpha families, so both speak of the whole group. For the theorem: Toda's pairs $ab_2/AB_2$ stand at $(3,32)/(3,33)$, $(9,44)/(9,45)$, $(15,56)/(15,57)$, $(21,68)/(21,69)$, and the tables have all of them but $(9,45)$; every other pair $ab/AB$ of simple elements is in the table of §5.6. Most likely the table of §5.6 misses a dot, and ${}_3\pi_{54}(S^9)=\mathbf Z/9\oplus\mathbf Z/3$. $E_2$ does not decide it: $\dim E_2(S^9)$ in the stem 45 is 8, and the balance of the differentials works out either way. In the grid above the cell is left as in the table and marked red. It is not our misreading: the reviewer re-read the place independently.

Misprints in the text of §5 (no effect on the groups; marked [sic] in the text): $AAB_2$ for $ABB_2$ in (5.1.7); $ab_2^2$ twice in (5.1.8); “(13) of (5.5.1)” for (5.1.1) on p. 46; $\beta^4$ for $\beta_1^4$ and $y=b_2^2$ for $b^2b_2$ in (5.1.11); “und” in Proposition 5.3; $\pi^5_{7+k}$ for $\pi^7_{7+k}$ on p. 49; $H_p(\partial\alpha(\xi))$ in Lemma 5.2; the label $E^2$ for $E_2$ in the diagram of Theorem 5.4 (2), $k=53$; in the same diagram at $k=55$ the print has $\bullet=\bullet\hookleftarrow\bullet$, whereas the table of §5.6 and the rows $k=43,45$ of Theorem 5.3 give $\bullet\hookleftarrow\bullet=\bullet$; in the table of §5.6 the stable name at $k=49$ is $\alpha_1\beta_1\beta_2$ for $\alpha_1\beta_1^2\beta_2$ ((17) of (5.1.1)).

The scan: the page “(3) Let $\xi=\alpha_1(7)\circ\varphi(10)$ …” is printed twice (PDF 65 and 66, numbered 58 and 59, two printings of one text); in the table of §6.5 the chains of $k=74$ ($\beta_5$) and $k=75$ ($\mu$) run one symbol into the header “stable”, which changes no group.

Names, not numbers. Toda's stable generators and those of Ravenel's Table A3.2 have different names: $\epsilon'=\langle\alpha_1,\alpha_1,\beta_1^3\rangle$, $\epsilon_1=\beta_{3/2}$, $\epsilon_2=\beta_3$, $\varphi=x_{45}$, $\lambda=x_{68}$, $\mu=x_{75}$; the orders agree everywhere (check B). There is no disagreement with Toda 1962 or with the stable stems.
